drafted_from: tools/export-documents-to-files/tool-rows.json (tool:export-a-markdown-book-to-word), do-work/export-a-book.mjs, README.md (the book settings row), test/export-a-book.test.mjs, and the real definitions of list:settings and list:checks read from the account
start_here: Say to your AI: "Export my book rye-cookbook to Word. Its settings row is already in my settings list, and the checks branch bakery-book judges the words first." It runs the exporter on your computer and tells you whether the Word file was written or why it was blocked.

lists.label: Settings
lists.holds: One row per tool and scope; for a book the row names the manuscript, its role, the bytes it must have, the Word template, the output folder and the checks branch.
alike: a config table in a spreadsheet

lists.label: Checks
lists.holds: The tree of rules a text is judged against: a branch row for a kind of writing and check rows under it, each with the words it forbids and what it says.

instructions: 1. Pour the example rows into your own settings list (see pour), put the manuscript, the Word template and the output folder in the book's settings JSON, and set source_blake3 to the BLAKE3 of the manuscript bytes. For current prose also name checks_branch and keep the example check rows in your checks list.

2. Say "Export my book rye-cookbook to Word". The AI reads the row with tools:list, writes {"book_id":"rye-cookbook"} to a request file and runs the row's run command from the Workshop checkout with your records door.

3. Read the last line, {"result": ...}. status exported names the Word file; blocked gives the reason (changed source bytes, the checks failed or ask reading questions, missing writing evidence). Answer reading questions in answers and run again.
4. After an export render the Word file to PDF and run verify_book_against_its_source.py as the row says; passing proves coverage only, never author approval.

worked_examples.title: A current-prose book with a banned word is blocked before any Word file is made
worked_examples.ask: Export my book rye-cookbook to Word.
worked_examples.given: Read from tools/export-documents-to-files/do-work/export-a-book.mjs (the same path test/export-a-book.test.mjs runs: "current prose whose checks fail is blocked before any DOCX is written"), not run here against a real door. Command: node tools/records-door/do-work/run-with-stdio-mcp.mjs door-client.json tools/export-documents-to-files/do-work/export-a-book.mjs exportABook request.json, with request.json {"book_id":"rye-cookbook"}. The settings row above gives role current_prose and checks_branch bakery-book; the manuscript holds the line "Some glitter here."; list:checks holds the no-glitter check with words ["glitter"] under bakery-writing, which bakery-book is part of.
worked_examples.hands_back: {"result":{"status":"blocked","reason":"The book's checks answered failed; no DOCX was created.","checks":{"branch":"bakery-book","lineage":["bakery-book","bakery-writing"],"status":"failed","passed":false}}} (checks also carries document_blake3 and the lines that failed); no .docx file is written.

pour.how: Name the settings list you already keep and its fields. The tool matches the kit's fields to yours by id, label or alike name, refuses under least_coverage, and otherwise answers the records:write that adds the example rows, leaving yours untouched.
